title: Hypothesis
description: A falsifiable claim about the codex or its corpus, bound to a test kind implemented in src/falsify.py.

id.description: H001..H008 are the original numbered series. H-ARCH-n and H-BYPASS belong to the architecture layer, which was added beside the numbered series rather than renumbering it.

statement.description: The claim, written so that a result can contradict it.

rationale.description: Why this is worth testing — what breaks if the claim is false.

prediction.description: What the run must show for the claim to survive. Stated before the run.

kind.description: Key into the TESTS registry in src/falsify.py.

params.description: Thresholds and settings. Changing these is a revision and belongs in the revisions array.

measures.description: CLAUDE.md RULE 1. A hypothesis is an attempt to measure a TARGET through a RENDERING. Falsifying the rendering does not close the target. When a hypothesis carrying this block is falsified, src/falsify.py raises target_question as an open unknown, unless target_reached is true.

target.description: What this is trying to measure.

rendering.description: The specific method or claim that carries the attempt, and the thing a falsification lands on.

target_question.description: The target written as a question, for the unknowns register.

target_reached.description: True only when the test reaches the target itself and not merely its rendering. Default false. Setting it true suppresses the auto-raise, so it is a claim and belongs in revisions if it changes.

status.description: Written by the engine on each run. 'open' means never run. 'no_data' means the test ran and could not reach a verdict — distinct from both other outcomes, and never counted as a pass.

revisions.description: Edits made to the claim after a falsification. Append only; the ledger holds the runs that forced them.

last_result.description: Written by the engine. The ledger is the durable record; this is a convenience.

passed.description: true supported, false falsified, null no data.
